OneKey Founder: Some Older iPhones Have Unpatchable Chip Vulnerabilities, Posing Risks to Seed Phrase Storage OneKey founder Yishi warned that factory-resetting an older iPhone, enabling airplane mode, and using it to store crypto wallet seed phrases offline may still be unsafe. He noted that iPhone 4S through iPhone X are affected by checkm8, while iPhone XS, XR, 11 series, and second-generation iPhone SE are affected by usbliter8, disclosed earlier this year. These BootROM-level vulnerabilities cannot be fixed through iOS updates. Attackers with physical access and specialized tools may exploit them via USB, even in airplane mode. However, on models such as the XS and 11, these flaws alone do not provide direct access to seed phrases, as device passcodes and the Secure Enclave offer additional protection. Yishi advised affected users to generate entirely new seed phrases in a trusted environment, transfer their assets, use newer devices, keep software updated, and adopt stronger passwords. — link

China’s Communist Party Calls for Crackdown on Corruption Using Crypto and Blockchain China’s Communist Party called for resolutely combating corruption committed via the internet, virtual currency, cross-border capital and blockchain, according to a resolution adopted at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee on October 29. The document also calls for stronger efforts to investigate cross-border corruption and recover illicit assets. — link

Issuer Objections to OKXICE Tokenized Stocks Expand to 50 Companies The number of companies objecting to the tokenization of their shares on OKXICE TSV, a joint venture between OKX and NYSE parent ICE, has risen to 50, with Nvidia, Micron, Nike, Costco and Reddit among the latest additions. OKXICE had initially planned to offer tokenized trading in shares of 62 companies. Under the SEC’s temporary conditional exemption, issuers may submit a written objection within 30 calendar days of receiving notice to prevent tokenized versions of their shares, issued by an unaffiliated third party, from being traded on the venue. — link

Binance Attacker Moved About $242 Million via Tron Within Two Days; Over $3 Billion in Stolen Assets Remain Largely Untouched According to on-chain analyst SomaXBT, about two days after the Binance attack, the attacker transferred approximately $242 million through Tron-related paths. In the incident, roughly $628 million in assets on Tron were stolen. After Tether froze about 378.7 million USDT, the attacker moved funds via Relay, THORChain, Chainflip, Symbiosis and other channels. An additional approximately $41.7 million flowed through Bitget Wallet, with its destination still unconfirmed. About $7.5 million remains on Tron, while more than $3 billion in stolen assets held by the attacker on other chains have largely remained unmoved. — link
